info.name: SeatCraft API
info.description:
Exam seat allocation and admit-card engine.

## Run order
Folders are numbered. Run top to bottom (Collection Runner or `newman run`). Later folders depend on ids captured by earlier ones.

## Prerequisites
- API running: `cd backend && dotnet run --project src/SeatCraft.Api`
- Environment **SeatCraft - Local** selected
- Run from the `postman/` folder so the CSV fixture paths resolve

## Re-runnable
`Register Tenant` accepts **409** when the tenant already exists, and the following `Login` obtains a token either way. The collection can be run repeatedly against the same database.

## Captured variables
Written to the **environment**: `token`, `examId`, `institutionId`, `hallId`, `hallBId`, `candidateId`, `runId`, `greedyRunId`, `planId`, `candidateA`, `candidateB`, `seededExamId`, `seededRunId`.

## Note on assertions
The solver guarantees no *same-institution adjacency* violations. Roll-order is advisory and may be reported without blocking publish, so tests assert on blocking violations only.

request.description:
Self-repeating request. The pre-request script picks the next code (C2 to C6) and the test script calls `pm.execution.setNextRequest` until all five exist.

This is the canonical Postman looping pattern and works in both Postman and Newman.

item.name: 06 - Allocation
item.description: The core flow: start an async run, poll until terminal, then work with the resulting plan.

header.description: Optional. Repeated calls with the same key return the same run instead of starting another.

request.description:
Strategies:
- `Greedy` - naive first fit, may leave adjacency conflicts
- `Balanced` - DSATUR ordering, usually clean
- `Strict` - repair pass, aims for zero violations (default choice)

Returns **409 Conflict** if another run is already active for this exam.

exec: pm.test('run finished within 30 polls', () => pm.expect.fail('Still ' + body.status + ' after 30 polls'));
console.log('Plan ' + body.resultSeatPlanId + ' - ' + body.candidateCount + ' candidates in ' + body.hallsUsed + ' hall(s), ' + body.durationMs + ' ms, ' + body.bestViolationCount + ' violation(s)');

request.description: Polls until the run leaves Queued/Running, re-invoking itself with `pm.execution.setNextRequest`. Caps at 30 attempts so a stuck run fails instead of looping forever.

Same data, weaker strategy. With many institutions relative to seats Greedy often looks fine; the gap appears when a few institutions dominate the roster. Use the demo seed in folder 12 to make the contrast stark.

exec: pm.test('cancel accepted or run already finished', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 409]));

request.description: Cancelling an already-completed run returns **409** - expected, and why this test accepts both codes.

item.name: 07 - Seat Plans
item.description: Inspect the generated plan, make manual overrides, publish, and verify immutability.

exec: console.log('Note: roll-order advisory reported - non-blocking by design.');

request.description:
Full plan with every assignment plus a re-validated violation list.

Only *blocking* violations (same-institution adjacency) prevent publishing. Roll-order is reported as advisory.
Runs the independent validator over the stored plan.

exec: console.log('Swap blocked: would introduce ' + body.violationCount + ' violation(s). The forced variant below shows the override path.');

request.description: The system re-validates immediately. If the swap breaks a rule it returns `applied: false` with the specific violations instead of saving a broken plan.

exec: console.log(body.applied ? 'Forced override applied and audited.' : 'No violations existed, so no force was needed.');

request.description: `force=true` plus a reason lets an operator save a plan that breaks a rule. The override is written to the audit trail with the reason attached.

exec: pm.test('200 OK or 409 if seat taken', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 409]));

request.description: Moves a candidate to a specific seat. Returns **409** if that seat is occupied - swap instead. Either outcome is valid here depending on the generated plan.
Seat coordinates outside the hall layout are rejected before anything is written.

Publishing makes seats visible to candidates via the public lookup. Any previously published plan is superseded.

Returns **409** if blocking violations remain.
A published plan is frozen, so candidates never see a plan that changed under them.
